BELMONTE VOWS FLOOD-FREE, INCLUSIVE QUEZON CITY IN FINAL TERM

Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte on Monday, June 30, took her oath of office and vowed to pursue broader reforms aimed at making the city more inclusive, resilient, and prepared for future challenges as she enters her third and final term.

In her inaugural speech, Belmonte committed to making the next three years the best for QCitizens by enhancing public service delivery, improving infrastructure, and addressing the city's longstanding flooding problems. "Together, we will build a Quezon City that is not only stronger and more progressive, but also kinder and more hopeful," she said.

Among her key priorities is the full implementation of flood control projects across all districts, including slope protection, detention basins, and water drainage systems, in coordination with district representatives.

Belmonte also outlined plans to register all QCitizens under the PhilHealth Konsulta program, build a new hospital in District 6, expand facilities at the Quezon City General Hospital, and strengthen the city’s social protection and livelihood services.

To sustain economic growth, she reaffirmed the city's pro-business stance, highlighting that more businesses mean more job opportunities. Her administration also plans to double local scholarship slots, expand the QCity Bus Service with electric buses, and modernize city infrastructure—from parks and open spaces to barangay health centers and safer pedestrian walkways.

Cultural and tourism investments, enhanced police mobility, and a shift toward service-driven governance rooted in empathy and transparency are also part of her agenda.

"Malinaw ang mandato na ipinagkaloob ng mga mamamayan," Belmonte said. "Pahiwatig ito na tama ang landas na ating tinatahak at nararamdaman na ng ating mga kababayan ang mga pagbabagong ating pinagsikapan."
